articles.title: Paige Bueckers joins rare company as Dallas Wings surge toward playoffs
articles.standfirst: The performance was another example of the all-around excellence that has transformed
articles.summary: The performance was another example of the all-around excellence that has transformed
articles.body:
Paige Bueckers arrived in the WNBA carrying enormous expectations. Less than two full seasons later, she is doing something even more impressive: exceeding them. The Dallas Wings superstar added another chapter to her rapidly growing legacy on Saturday night, leading her team to an 87-82 victory over the Phoenix Mercury while setting a new WNBA scoring milestone that further cemented her place among the league's brightest stars.

Bueckers finished with a game-high 26 points, four rebounds, five assists, three steals, and one block as Dallas secured its sixth consecutive victory. The performance was another example of the all-around excellence that has transformed the former UConn standout from a highly touted prospect into one of the most impactful players in professional basketball.

The win also came on a historic night

During the game, Bueckers became the highest-scoring player through the first two seasons of a WNBA career . The league announced the achievement on social media shortly after the milestone was reached.

“History. Made: Paige Bueckers has scored the most points (1,515) by any player through their first two seasons in WNBA history!”

The record is notable not only because of the names Bueckers passed, but because of what those names represent. She moved ahead of Hall of Famer Seimone Augustus, who scored 1,513 points through her first two seasons, and surpassed WNBA legend Cynthia Cooper, one of the greatest scorers the sport has ever seen.

Bueckers has benefited from the WNBA's expanded 44-game schedule that began during her rookie season in 2025. Augustus established her mark in 68 games, while Cooper accumulated her total in just 58 contests. Even with that caveat, the accomplishment underscores a reality that has become impossible to ignore.

Bueckers is one of the most gifted offensive players in the sport

She reached the milestone in 75 career games and still has two regular-season contests remaining. More importantly, she has paired her scoring ability with elite playmaking, defensive activity, and leadership, turning herself into the centerpiece of a Dallas team that appears to be peaking at exactly the right time. The six-game winning streak is evidence of that growth.

After spending much of the season fighting for playoff positioning, the Wings have surged into the postseason conversation with momentum on their side. Dallas currently sits at 26-16 and occupies sixth place in the standings with road games remaining against Phoenix and Seattle before the playoffs begin. Bueckers has been the driving force behind that rise.

What makes her ascent especially intriguing is the company she is beginning to keep. For much of the past several years, conversations about the league's biggest stars have centered around players such as A'ja Wilson, Breanna Stewart, Napheesa Collier, and, more recently, Caitlin Clark. Wilson remains one of the most dominant two-way players in basketball, while Clark has become one of the most influential stars the WNBA has ever seen thanks to her scoring, passing, and ability to transform an offense.

The reigning Rookie of the Year has already become a two-time All-Star and a FIBA Women's Basketball World Cup gold medalist . More importantly, she has demonstrated the ability to impact every facet of the game. On Saturday alone, she scored efficiently, facilitated the offense, generated turnovers, and protected the rim. Few guards in the league offer that complete package.

articles.title: Angel Reese makes history as Wendell Carter Jr. celebrates in style
articles.summary: Angel Reese's record-breaking 2026 season reached another historic milestone Saturday night, and Wendell Carter Jr. was there to celebrate it in style. The Atlanta Dream star became the first player in WNBA history to collect 500 rebounds in a single season during Atlanta's 106-81 victory over the Chicago Sky. Reese finished with 23 points, 10 rebounds, four assists, three blocks and two steals, helping the Dream secure their eighth win in their last 10 games and strengthen their position heading into the postseason. And after the game, Carter once again made sure the spotlight stayed on Reese. The NBA big man, who has become one of Reese's most visible supporters, was spotted rocking another custom Angel Reese jersey following her latest historic performance. It was a fitting celebration for a player who continues to rewrite the WNBA record book in just her third professional season.

articles.title: Caitlin Clark and the Fever steal the spotlight before disappointing home game
articles.standfirst: Indiana had a tough afternoon against Washington, although Caitlin Clark, Sophie Cunningham and Lexie Hull still found a way to turn heads before the game.
articles.summary: Indiana had a tough afternoon against Washington, although Caitlin Clark, Sophie Cunningham and Lexie Hull still found a way to turn heads before the game.
articles.body:
This Sunday, the Indiana Fever faced the Washington Mystics at Gainbridge Fieldhouse in a game that ended with a 93-77 Washington victory. Caitlin Clark led Indiana in scoring with 25 points, along with 5 assists, 2 rebounds and 2 steals. Kelsey Mitchell added 22 points, while Lexie Hull finished with 2 points and 2 rebounds .

For Sophie Cunningham, the afternoon was even tougher. She came off the bench and played seven minutes without recording any points, rebounds or assists.

So, if there was anything the Fever could brag about that afternoon, it had to happen before the game even started. Caitlin Clark, Sophie Cunningham and Lexie Hull arrived at the arena in completely different looks and managed to turn some heads before tipoff .

Caitlin Clark went with burgundy

Clark arrived at Gainbridge Fieldhouse in a sporty look centered around burgundy.

The player wore Nike sweatpants with a white T-shirt from the same brand . She added a white-and-burgundy fleece jacket on top, while her sneakers followed the same color combination.

Dark sunglasses, her hair worn down and a few accessories completed the look she chose for her arrival at the game.

Sophie Cunningham completely changed things up

Cunningham showed up in a much more dressed-up combination. The player opted for a dark brown polo shirt with a gray-and-white skirt .

She completed the look with heels, a black handbag, dark sunglasses and a necklace, while leaving her hair down.

The result was quite different from Clark's sporty outfit, showing that there was more than one way to arrive at the same game.

Lexie Hull found the middle ground

Hull arrived in a white blouse and dark brown shorts, paired with a belt in a lighter shade of brown .

Open-toe heels, a handbag and dark sunglasses completed the outfit, while she also wore her hair down.

Her look landed somewhere between the previous two: dressier than Clark's sporty outfit, but not quite as dressed up as Cunningham's.

Now the Fever will have to turn their attention to Minnesota

The loss to Washington is already behind them, and the Fever will not have much time to dwell on it. Indiana will be back in action on Tuesday, September 22, once again at Gainbridge Fieldhouse, this time against the Minnesota Lynx .

articles.title: Caitlin Clark’s violent screaming match with Stephanie White caught on camera
articles.standfirst: Caitlin Clark wasn’t holding back. The Fever star had a heated exchange with coach Stephanie White during a frustrating loss to the Mystics.
articles.summary: Caitlin Clark wasn’t holding back. The Fever star had a heated exchange with coach Stephanie White during a frustrating loss to the Mystics.
articles.body:
C aitlin Clar k once again became a topic of conversation after an interaction that may shed light on her relationship with her coach. The Indiana Feve r star shared a tense moment with head coach Stephanie White during the first quarter against the Washington Mystics , at a time when the team was already in trouble.

With Washington leading 31-17 and 58.7 seconds left in the opening period, Clark walked toward the defensive end, turned toward the bench, and expressed her frustration directly at White in full view of everyone .

The exchange stood out because it came just days after the coach had publicly praised her star’s leadership, even saying that Clark “sounds like a coach.”

As the first quarter neared its end, Clark waited for play to resume but used the moment to address White on the sideline. The coach listened while the Indiana point guard made her dissatisfaction clear.

The exchange reflected Clark’s competitive personality. She consistently takes on a leadership role on the court and does not hesitate to speak up when she believes corrections are needed.

The Mystics had taken complete control of the game. Washington closed the first quarter ahead 34-19 and went into halftime with a 51-30 lead .

Kiki Iriafen was key with 21 points and 14 rebounds, while Shakira Austin added 20 points and 10 rebounds in the 93-77 victory.

For Indiana, Clark finished with 25 points and five assists, and Kelsey Mitchell scored 22 points , but the team never mounted a comeback. With two games remaining, Washington moved to within one game of the Fever in the race for the fifth seed.

articles.title: Caitlin Clark's frustration: Why the Fever's "lamentable" defensive effort could backfire
articles.standfirst: Indiana's 93-77 loss to Washington exposed defensive problems at the worst possible time, with the Fever now facing the league-leading Minnesota Lynx twice to close the regular season
articles.summary: Indiana's 93-77 loss to Washington exposed defensive problems at the worst possible time, with the Fever now facing the league-leading Minnesota Lynx twice to close the regular season
articles.body:
The Indiana Fever had little time to enjoy their latest winning streak before running into a major warning sign heading into the WNBA playoffs.

After defeating the Toronto Tempo 103-85 on Friday, Indiana returned home Sunday expecting to build more momentum.

Instead, the Fever were overwhelmed by the Washington Mystics , falling 93-77 in a result that left Caitlin Clark visibly frustrated with the team's defensive execution.

Clark still produced 25 points, five assists, two steals and a block, while Kelsey Mitchell contributed 22 points. But Indiana's offense could not compensate for the team's inability to contain Washington , particularly during a disastrous opening stretch.

The Mystics established control almost immediately, opening the game with a 16-8 advantage. Indiana never found a consistent response and eventually fell behind by as many as 26 points.

Washington shot 57% from the field while limiting the Fever to 37%, according to the Associated Press, highlighting the disparity between the two teams on the afternoon.

The problem was not confined to one unit, either. Washington's starters outscored Indiana's starters 74-69, while the Mystics ' reserves also had the upper hand, winning the bench battle 19-8.

For Clark , the most concerning aspect was the way the Fever allowed Washington to gain confidence so quickly.

“I think when you give a team that type of confidence early in the game, you’re just digging yourself a huge hole, and a hole we could never climb out of,” Clark said.

“And, you know, I thought we were just sloppy, sloppy in everything we were trying to execute. I don’t know, our defense was just pitiful and it was frustrating.”

Her comments came after one of Indiana's poorest performances of the season and at a particularly important point in the playoff race.

The Fever entered Sunday sitting fifth in the standings at 27-14 and remained fifth after the defeat, now 27-15. Washington improved to 26-16 and moved within one game of Indiana.

That positioning matters because Indiana is attempting to finish inside the top four, which would provide home-court advantage in the opening playoff round.

The Lynx present an immediate defensive test

Clark was also careful to acknowledge that Washington deserved credit for its performance. She described the Mystics' display as “really beautiful basketball,” but the compliment did not disguise what she believed went wrong for Indiana.

The Fever surrendered 50 points in the paint, an area that Clark specifically highlighted after the game.

“We got to be able to have a coverage in certain things that we can stop them,” Clark added.

That issue could become even more important immediately because Indiana's final two regular-season games are against Minnesota.

The Lynx entered the final stretch of the regular season with the league's best record and moved to 32-10 after defeating Connecticut 101-89 on Sunday. Minnesota also remains in contention for the No. 1 overall seed, making the closing stretch particularly significant.

The Fever and Lynx are scheduled to meet Tuesday, Sept. 22, in Indiana before finishing the regular-season series in Minnesota on Thursday, Sept. 24.

The WNBA's official schedule confirms the back-to-back meetings to close Indiana's regular season.

Indiana already knows how difficult Minnesota can be. The teams met in August, when the Lynx defeated the Fever 108-100 in Minneapolis.

That makes Clark's criticism about the defensive performance particularly relevant. Indiana cannot afford to give another high-level opponent the sort of early confidence Washington found on Sunday, especially against a Minnesota team fighting for the league's top playoff position.

The Fever still have an opportunity to repair the situation before the postseason begins. But the Washington defeat demonstrated how quickly defensive lapses can turn into a runaway deficit.

For a team trying to secure a top-four position, the final two games therefore represent more than routine regular-season contests. They will give Indiana a chance to test whether the problems Clark identified can be corrected before the games become even more consequential.

And with the Lynx waiting, the Fever will not have to wait long to find out.

articles.title: Where to watch Atlanta Dream vs New York Liberty? TV channel and game time for Angel Reese’s team
articles.standfirst: Atlanta Dream bring East's best record to Barclays for Liberty Clash
articles.summary: Atlanta Dream bring East's best record to Barclays for Liberty Clash
articles.body:
The last games of the regular season arrive at Barclays Center on Monday night as the New York Liberty host the Atlanta Dream, a matchup between two of the Eastern Conference's heavyweights that promises to set the tone for the WNBA Playoffs.

This is a collision of experience and momentum — a Liberty side chasing another deep run against an Atlanta team that finished the regular season as the top club in the East.

When and where to watch the Atlanta Dream vs New York Liberty?

Tip-off is scheduled for the early hours of Monday, 21 September 2026 at 8:00 p.m. Eastern Time (7:00 p.m. Central Time and 5:00 p.m. Pacific Time). The game is staged at the Barclays Center in Brooklyn, a venue with a capacity of 18,732.

American audiences can find WNBA coverage across different TV channels and streaming services; however for this game between Atlanta and New York, you’ll be able to watch it on NBCSN and Peacock.

Two contenders, separated by fine margins

The regular-season table tells a story of near-equals. Atlanta tops the Eastern Conference with a 28–14 record, edging out a crowded pack behind them. New York is currently third in the East at 26–16, a game and a half back but every bit as dangerous.

Looking at the wider league picture and the two sides are practically inseparable: Atlanta sits fourth overall and New York seventh, but both carried 24 points in the combined standings, underlining just how tight this bracket has become.

The numbers reinforce that. Atlanta was one of the most productive offensive teams in the conference, pouring in 3,841 points across the season while conceding 3,568 — a points differential of +273 that ranked among the best in the East.

New York's profile is more measured: 3,792 scored against 3,624 allowed for a +168 differential. The Dream have the sharper margin, but the Liberty's championship-tested core means these season totals only tell part of the tale.

New York Liberty: star power and continuity

The Liberty roster remains stacked with elite talent. Sabrina Ionescu runs the show from the backcourt, flanked by the versatility of Breanna Stewart and Satou Sabally up front, with Jonquel Jones anchoring the interior.

That quartet gives head-office belief that New York can trade blows with anyone in a seven-game or single-elimination format. Germany's Leonie Fiebich adds two-way length on the wing, while the backcourt has a distinct international flavour with France's Marine Johannes, Marine Fauthoux and Pauline Astier all on the books.

The frontcourt depth is a genuine asset. Alongside Jones, New York can lean on the size of Han Xu and Spain's Raquel Carrera, and the athleticism of Rebecca Allen and Australia's Anneli Maley on the wing. With home-court advantage in Brooklyn and a raucous Barclays crowd behind them, the Liberty will want to impose their pace and physicality from the opening whistle.

Atlanta Dream: the East's form team

Atlanta earned their conference crown on the strength of a balanced, deep group. Allisha Gray and Rhyne Howard form one of the most dynamic scoring backcourts in the league, capable of taking over stretches on their own. Veteran DeWanna Bonner brings postseason scars and steadiness, while Jordin Canada offers speed and disruption at the point of attack.

The Dream frontcourt is where much of the intrigue lies. Angel Reese has become a magnet for attention on the glass and around the rim, and she is paired with the interior toughness of Brionna Jones and the energy of Naz Hillmon.

Mali's Sika Kone and Kenya's Madina Okot add further length inside, giving Atlanta a rotation that can go big or spread the floor with shooters like Te-Hina Paopao. The rebounding battle between Reese, Brionna Jones and New York's Jonquel Jones could well decide possessions in a game this closely matched.

Players to watch during the Atlanta Dream vs New York Liberty game

Sabrina Ionescu (New York): The engine of the Liberty offence, equally capable of orchestrating for others or shouldering the scoring load when the game tightens. In a series this fine, her decision-making down the stretch could be the difference.

Allisha Gray (Atlanta): The Dream's leading scoring threat and a two-way handful, Gray sets the tone for Atlanta's transition game and will be central to any road success at Barclays.

Angel Reese (Atlanta): Her work on the offensive glass creates second-chance points that can quietly swing tight postseason games. If she wins her battle inside, Atlanta's ceiling rises considerably.

Prediction for the Atlanta Dream vs New York Liberty game

This has the makings of a coin-flip. Atlanta arrive with the better regular-season record and the sharper points differential, but New York's home floor, championship experience and elite top-end talent are difficult to bet against in a Barclays Center opener. Expect a physical, high-possession contest decided in the final minutes — and a narrow New York win to set an early tone in the game.

articles.standfirst: Kelsey Plum's Mercury Host Paige Bueckers and the Wings
articles.summary: Kelsey Plum's Mercury Host Paige Bueckers and the Wings
articles.body:
The 2026 regular season told contrasting stories for these clubs and this Monday night, Paige Bueckers’ Dallas Wings play one of their last games of the 2026 regular season at against the Pheonix Mercury.

The Dallas Wings finished at 26-16, landing fourth in the Western Conference and holding a healthy scoring margin — 3,744 points scored against 3,573 conceded, a plus-171 differential across 42 games. That balance of offense and defense marks them as a genuine threat.

Phoenix, by contrast, backed into this matchup the hard way. The Mercury closed the year 15-27, seventh in the West, and were outscored on the season (3,543 for, 3,668 against, a minus-125 differential).

On paper, Dallas arrives as the favorite. But the Footprint Centre can be a difficult place to play, and Phoenix has the individual talent to swing any single night.

Where to watch the Dallas vs Phoenix game and what time is staring

The Phoenix Mercury are playing their last regular season game at home against the Dallas Wings this Monday, September 22, tipping off at 10:00 p.m. Eastern Time (9:00 p.m. Central Time and 7:00 p.m. Pacific Time) at the Footprint Centre in Phoenix.

It's a matchup that pits backcourt star power against playoff experience, and both rosters are stacked with names capable of taking over a game.

American viewers can catch the action across the WNBA's including the Dallas vs Pheonix game at USA Network and streaming with the WNBA League Pass.

Dallas Wings vs Phoenix Mercury Rosters and players to watch: Star Power on Both Sides

This game is loaded with recognizable names. For Phoenix, guard Kelsey Plum headlines a backcourt that also features veteran Sami Whitcomb. The Mercury's frontcourt carries serious pedigree in Alyssa Thomas, one of the league's most versatile forwards, alongside scoring wing Kahleah Copper. That trio gives Phoenix the kind of two-way firepower that can neutralize a talent gap over 40 minutes of basketball.

Dallas counters with a young, dynamic guard rotation. Paige Bueckers, at 24, leads the way alongside sharpshooter Azzi Fudd and dangerous scorer Arike Ogunbowale, whose ability to erupt from the perimeter can flip a game in a matter of possessions. Up front, Alanna Smith and Jessica Shepard provide size and rebounding, while veteran Alysha Clark brings championship-tested composure to the wing.

The clash of styles is fascinating: Dallas leans on youthful pace and outside shooting, while Phoenix relies on the physicality and playoff nous of Thomas, Copper, and Plum.

The single most compelling subplot is the guard duel. Bueckers and Fudd represent the Wings' present and future, a pairing built for tempo and three-point volume. Phoenix will lean on Plum to answer shot-for-shot — she's the kind of scorer who thrives on the postseason stage, and the burden of keeping the Mercury afloat offensively will fall largely on her shoulders.

If Ogunbowale gets hot from deep, Dallas becomes very hard to stop. Conversely, if Thomas can dominate the glass and control the pace, she can drag Phoenix into the kind of half-court grind that suits the Mercury far more than the Wings.

Paige Bueckers (Dallas): The 24-year-old guard is the engine of the Wings' attack. How she handles the pressure of the moment against a veteran Phoenix defense could define the series.

Kelsey Plum (Phoenix): The Mercury's go-to scorer. If Phoenix is going to pull the upset, Plum almost certainly has to deliver a big night.

Alyssa Thomas (Phoenix): A do-everything forward whose rebounding, passing, and defense can tilt the tempo. When Thomas is engaged, Phoenix plays a level up.

Arike Ogunbowale (Dallas): A volume scorer capable of a single-handed run that puts a game out of reach.

The numbers favor Dallas. The Wings are currently with a far superior record and a positive scoring margin, while Phoenix limped to the finish line and was outscored on the year.

Expect the Wings' young backcourt to test a Mercury defense that leaked points all season. That said, Phoenix has the star quality — Plum, Thomas, and Copper — to make this a genuine fight, and home court at a packed Footprint Centre is worth something.

The lean here is Dallas to take the opener, but don't be surprised if Phoenix's veterans keep it close deep into the fourth quarter. A high-scoring, guard-driven affair looks likely — one where the last few possessions decide it.

articles.title: Caitlin Clark watches Sophie Cunningham’s role shrink as the Fever prepare for the WNBA playoffs
articles.standfirst: The Fever suffered their first double-digit loss since July in their last game against Washington
articles.summary: The Fever suffered their first double-digit loss since July in their last game against Washington
articles.body:
The 30th WNBA regular season is coming to an end this week with Thursday being the last day of action before the playoffs begin on September 27th with the first round being a best-of-three series.

Although the eight playoff-bound teams ( Lynx , Valkyries , Aces , Dream , Fever , Liberty , Wings , Mystics ) have been locked in for weeks, exact seeding remains undecided with only two games left, featuring a tight race for positions six through eight and the second-place Valkyries hunting down Minnesota at the top of the table.

For the league's most popular franchise, the Indiana Fever, the final stretch is intensely demanding with their last two matchups pitting them against the top-seeded Minnesota Lynx both at home and on the road.

Right now, the Fever sit in fifth place in the overall standings, but can finish as low as the eighth seed or as high as third depending on this week's results.

Sophie Cunningham and Lexie Hull See Playing Time Dip

In the Fever's last outing , the team stumbled in a 93-77 defeat to the Washington Mystics, marking their first double-digit loss since July 15 and the first time they scored fewer than 80 points since that same mid-July stumble against the Valkyries.

The tactical adjustments led to notable shifts in playing time, with sharpshooters Lexie Hull and Sophie Cunningham seeing their roles shrink significantly. Hull struggled to find a rhythm and was benched at halftime in favor of rookie Raven Johnson , finishing with just 13 minutes of action.

Meanwhile, Cunningham, typically Indiana's primary sparkplug off the bench, logged a mere 7 minutes on the floor and went 0-for-2 from the field , failing to record a point, rebound, or assist.

Speaking to reporters after the game, coach White addressed what she needs from the supporting cast moving forward: "We've got to get them the ball in positions to get good shots, and make shots. And they've got to help us on the defensive end and rebounding the basketball."

Caitlin Clark and Kelsey Mitchell Lead Record-Breaking Offense

Even with the setback, Indiana boasts the most explosive offense in league history , averaging 96.7 points per game with a record 20 games scoring over 100 points .

Spearheaded by Kelsey Mitchell (averaging 25.1 points per game , second-best in the WNBA) and maestro Caitlin Clark , who is orchestrating the most offensively productive season in league history as the third-best scorer ( 22.7 PPG ) and assist leader ( 8.4 APG ), the superstar backcourt combined for another milestone.

During the loss, both players crossed the 20-point threshold , extending their shared WNBA single-season record to 21 games with 20+ points each.

However, a brutal defensive start and early offensive stagnation, compounded by foul trouble for Aliyah Boston , exposed vulnerabilities against a tough Mystics frontline, prompting head coach Stephanie White to aggressively adjust her rotations.

As the postseason approaches, tightening rotations is expected, but the recent struggles underscore a glaring reality: the Fever remain heavily reliant on their elite trio of Clark, Mitchell, and Boston , all of whom are premier All-Star talents ranked among the league's top-tier performers.

articles.title: WNBA History: Caitlin Clark silences critics with a legendary scoring milestone
articles.standfirst: The Fever star became the highest-scoring point guard in a single season
articles.summary: The Fever star became the highest-scoring point guard in a single season
articles.body:
Caitlin Clark didn't need long to remind the WNBA that one broken rookie record does not diminish the scale of what she is building in Indiana.

Olivia Miles had just moved past Clark ’s rookie scoring total with another standout performance for the Minnesota Lynx .

Only hours later, Clark produced a milestone of her own, reaching 862 points this season and setting a new single-season scoring record for a WNBA point guard.

Clark got there after scoring 25 points against the Washington Mystics , continuing a remarkable third professional season in which she has averaged 22.7 points per game while shooting 45.1 percent from the field.

The record also highlights just how much more efficient Clark has become since her rookie campaign. She reached 862 points in 38 games. Her previous rookie total of 769 came across 40 appearances.

Miles takes one of Clark’s rookie records

The timing made the achievement even more striking. Earlier in the day, Miles entered Minnesota’s game against the Connecticut Sun tied with Clark ’s rookie scoring mark of 769 points.

She moved ahead with a second-quarter free throw and finished with 21 points in the Lynx ’s 101-89 victory, lifting her season total to 790.

“It’s special, but it means we’re more so working well as a team,” Miles said afterward. “I have great teammates around me, great vets who allow me to be me out there.”

Miles also pointed to Minnesota’s support system as a major factor in her rapid rise.

“It wouldn’t be possible without one, a coach that believes in you and then two, having teammates that have my back,” she said. “So it’s really special to obviously be able to accomplish that with such a great team and on a win as well.”

Miles has taken more than one rookie mark from Clark this season. She hit eight three-pointers against the Golden State Valkyries in June, surpassing Clark ’s rookie single-game record of seven, and became the fastest rookie to reach 350 points, 100 rebounds and 100 assists.

Clark’s latest record moves conversation

Clark ’s response came in a different category entirely. Her 862 points represent the most ever by a point guard in a single WNBA season, moving her beyond comparisons with her own rookie year and into the league’s broader record book.

That gives the final two regular-season meetings between Indiana and Minnesota an added layer of intrigue. Clark and Miles are scheduled to meet in Indiana on September 22 before the teams close the season in Minneapolis two days later.

Minnesota is fighting to secure the No.1 seed, while Indiana is still trying to strengthen its playoff position. The individual storyline will be difficult to ignore.

Miles has already erased several of Clark ’s rookie records. Clark , meanwhile, is now setting marks that apply to every point guard who has played in the league.

articles.standfirst: Indiana’s home finale carries major playoff implications against the team with the WNBA’s best record
articles.summary: Indiana’s home finale carries major playoff implications against the team with the WNBA’s best record
articles.body:
The Indiana Fever have reached the stage of the season where every result can reshape the WNBA playoff picture, and Tuesday night brings one of their toughest tests yet.

Indiana welcomes the Minnesota Lynx to Gainbridge Fieldhouse on Tuesday, September 22, with tipoff set for 8 p.m. ET. The game will be shown nationally on ESPN, giving viewers across the country a chance to watch Caitlin Clark and the Fever take on the team currently sitting atop the WNBA standings.

The stakes are high for both sides. Indiana enters the matchup at 27-15 and fifth in the standings, still chasing a top-four finish that would secure home-court advantage in the first round. Minnesota is 32-10 and trying to protect the No.1 seed as the regular season winds down.

Is Caitlin Clark playing against the Lynx?

Clark is listed as probable with a back issue, meaning she is expected to play unless her status changes closer to tipoff. Her presence would be significant for an Indiana team trying to respond after a heavy loss to the Washington Mystics .

Clark is averaging 22.7 points, 8.4 assists and 3.9 rebounds this season while shooting 45.1 percent from the field and 36.8 percent from three-point range.

She remains one of the central figures in an offense that also features Kelsey Mitchell and Aliyah Boston . Mitchell enters the game averaging 25.1 points, while Boston has contributed 16.4 points and 8.1 rebounds per game.

Minnesota have the league’s best record

The Lynx have been driven by one of the WNBA’s biggest rookie stories. Olivia Miles is averaging 19.8 points, 6.0 assists and 4.7 rebounds while shooting 38.8 percent from three-point range.

Her emergence has helped Minnesota remain at the top of the league despite entering the season with major questions around its roster. Napheesa Collier and Kayla McBride remain key parts of the Lynx attack, giving Minnesota multiple scoring threats heading into Indianapolis.

The matchup also carries extra intrigue because Clark and Miles are two of the league’s most closely watched guards, with Miles recently breaking several rookie records previously held by Clark .

How to watch Lynx vs Fever

The game begins at 8 p.m. ET / 7 p.m. CT on Tuesday, September 22, at Gainbridge Fieldhouse.

Streaming: Available through participating services carrying ESPN

The teams will meet again only two days later in Minnesota, creating a rare back-to-back finish to the regular season between two teams with plenty still to play for.

Indiana could strengthen its push for home-court advantage with a win. Minnesota, meanwhile, has the chance to tighten its grip on the No.1 seed.

articles.summary: Dallas has won more matches this season than in the previous two seasons combined
articles.body:
With the WNBA regular season wrapping up this week, all 15 teams have just one or two games left and the eight clubs already in the playoffs still do not have their seeding locked.

At the top, the Minnesota Lynx ( 32-10 ) and Golden State Valkyries ( 31-11 ) are fighting for the No. 1 seed. One more Lynx win in their two remaining games against the Indiana Fever would give Minnesota the league’s best record for a second straight year.

Below them, the picture is messier. The New York Liberty and Dallas Wings both dropped their latest games and now sit together at 26-17, sliding toward a first-round date with one of the top teams instead of climbing into a more favorable spot.

Bueckers’ 30-Point Night Not Enough as Dallas Slips in the Standings

Paige Bueckers poured in 30 points and added seven assists on Monday, but the Dallas Wings still fell 87-86 to the Phoenix Mercury on Kahleah Copper’s layup with 2.4 seconds left.

The loss snapped a six-game winning streak and hurt Dallas’ shot at a top-six seed . The Wings have been in the postseason for weeks, and that alone marks a real step forward: Bueckers has guided them back after three seasons out of the playoffs .

She is averaging 20.8 points and 5.9 assists in 2026, set a franchise record with 853 points this year , and Dallas has already won more games this season than it did in the previous two combined. Still, the chance to move up vanished after the Liberty also lost earlier Monday to Atlanta.

If the season ended today, the Wings would be the No. 7 seed and open in San Francisco against Golden State.

Even a finale win over the last-place Seattle Storm (8-35) on Wednesday might not be enough. One more Liberty victory plus wins from the Washington Mystics and Fever could drop Dallas to eighth. Whoever they draw, the first-round series will be a grind.

articles.title: Caitlin Clark makes a big announcement as her star power takes center stage for the WNBA playoffs
articles.standfirst: Before Clark arrived, the Fever had missed the playoffs for seven consecutive seasons. With her, they haven't missed
articles.summary: Before Clark arrived, the Fever had missed the playoffs for seven consecutive seasons. With her, they haven't missed
articles.body:
As the 30th WNBA playoffs draw closer, the first round opens Sept. 27 as a best-of-three, the eight teams already in ( Lynx, Valkyries, Aces, Dream, Fever, Liberty, Wings, Mystics ) have been locked in for weeks but the seeding is still up for grabs with two games left.

Golden State is chasing Minnesota for first place. The Lynx play the Indiana Fever on the road tonight and at home Thursday; one more Minnesota win would lock the top seed for a second straight year.

For Indiana, a win in those two games would keep them no lower than fifth. The way the bracket is shaping up, a first-round Fever vs. Dream series , Caitlin Clark against Angel Reese , looks like the most-watched matchup in league history.

Nike Caitlin 1 Drops as Fever Close the Regular Season

As the Fever get ready for their last home game of the regular season and the postseason that follows, their star and the league’s biggest name announced with Nike her first signature shoe: the Nike Caitlin 1 . It hits globally Thursday, Oct. 1, at $140 .

Clark spent the last few days teasing the debut on Instagram, posting close-ups of the “Racer Blue” pair. Brand-mate Travis Scott even helped unveil a black fashion edition, a sign of how big this launch is.

The shoe introduces Nike Opticast , a new upper made of cast polyurethane nodes built to Clark’s specs and her game. Expect to see the Caitlin 1 on the street and in pickup runs as soon as it drops.

Clark’s MVP-Level Season Sets Up a Historic Playoff Spotlight

That off-court heat matches what she is doing on the floor. After missing most of last season, Clark is an MVP candidate in a historic year. She is running the most productive offense in league history as the third-best scorer at 22.7 points per game and the assist leader at 8.4 per game .

No player has ever finished top five in both; in the two seasons she has stayed healthy, she is on track to finish first in assists, showing her court vision is unmatched.

A Fever-Dream series would put Clark vs. Reese in front of the biggest TV audience the WNBA has seen since both were drafted in 2024, a rivalry that started in the NCAA and still drives the ratings.

articles.title: Caitlin Clark marks her territory with a fiery reaction toward Stephanie White as frustration boils over
articles.standfirst: The Indiana Fever star's reaction on the court raised questions as her team struggled against Washington
articles.summary: The Indiana Fever star's reaction on the court raised questions as her team struggled against Washington
articles.body:
Much has been said about the tension between Caitlin Clark and Stephanie White, although the Indiana Fever star has repeatedly insisted that they have a good relationship and always have each other's backs. However, Clark's reactions toward her head coach on the court have left some fans questioning whether everything is as smooth as she claims.

Indiana struggled against the Washington Mystics, failing to capitalize on their opportunities while allowing their opponents to dictate the game. Washington carved through the Fever's defense throughout the night, repeatedly beating players off the dribble and finding open shots whenever Indiana failed to rotate properly.

Clark's frustration becomes impossible to ignore

As Indiana fell behind early in the opening quarter, Clark turned toward White and the Fever bench, raising her hand in frustration before taking an inbound pass . New angles captured the intensity of the moment, while broadcast microphones picked up the guard demanding better defensive rotations , revealing just how quickly things were spiraling on the floor.

Clark appeared to shout toward her coach and the bench, although the arena audio did not make her exact words entirely clear. The Fever were already in a difficult position, trailing the Mystics 31-17 with less than a minute remaining in the first quarter after allowing 34 points in the opening period.

The Fever's defensive problems put White under pressure

White has faced plenty of criticism from fans over her rotations and lineup decisions, but the pressure appears to be extending beyond the stands. Sophie Cunningham has also openly questioned the coach's demanding two-hour practice sessions on her podcast, admitting that her body was taking a beating.

The Fever eventually fell 93-77, with Clark finishing the night with 25 points and five assists. Despite her individual production, the guard acknowledged that Indiana had been sloppy and described the team's defense as pitiful , reflecting the scale of the problems that contributed to the loss.

With the playoffs approaching, t he heated exchange serves as another reminder of the frustration surrounding Indiana's performances. The Fever entered the season among the teams expected to contend, and they will need to address their defensive issues and find greater consistency as the postseason draws closer. The reactions on the court have added another layer to the scrutiny surrounding White and her decisions. Indiana now faces the challenge of turning those frustrations into improvements before its struggles begin to affect its playoff ambitions.

articles.title: Caitlin Clark sends Andy Reid her unreleased ‘Sea of Red’ sneakers and his reaction says it all
articles.standfirst: Andy Reid couldn’t hide his excitement after receiving Caitlin Clark’s unreleased signature sneakers inspired by the Chiefs’ iconic colors.
articles.summary: Andy Reid couldn’t hide his excitement after receiving Caitlin Clark’s unreleased signature sneakers inspired by the Chiefs’ iconic colors.
articles.body:
C aitlin Clark and the Indiana Fever are on their way to making their third consecutive playoff appearance despite suffering a lopsided loss to the Washington Mystics on Sunday. Washington jumped out to a 51-30 halftime lead and extended the margin to as many as 26 points before the final buzzer.

Despite the defeat, Clark finished the game with 25 points , although she struggled from the field, shooting just 6-of-20 and committing five turnovers. The shooting slump has not affected her overall season, as the Indiana star is averaging 22.7 points per game, the third-best mark in the WNBA , along with 8.4 assists (tied for the league lead) and 3.9 rebounds, while shooting 45.1% from the field, 36.8% from three-point range and 84.8% from the free-throw line.

Indiana still has two games remaining, both against the Minnesota Lynx, the league’s top team. The Fever currently sit in fifth place in the standings and would begin the playoffs on the road unless they can sweep Minnesota and receive help from other results, as only the top four seeds earn home-court advantage.

Caitlin Clark’s new sneaker arrives in Kansas City

However, the biggest storyline surrounding Clark this week has not come from the court, but rather from the release of her first signature sneaker: the Nike Caitlin 1 , which will be available worldwide on October 1 for $140, along with an 18-piece apparel collection.

One special edition of the shoe has already made its way to Kansas City ahead of its official release. The “Sea of Red” colorway, inspired by the colors of the Chiefs, was delivered to head coach Andy Reid, who became the first person to receive the new model.

“I got my new Caitlin 1 ‘Sea of Red’ right here, especially from Caitlin Clark. I appreciate you, girl. All the ladies of the WNBA, you guys are unbelievable. Keep going. Love watching you, Caitlin. I love the color. Look at these things. It’s the same color you wear, and here we are, Chiefs. Love it,” Reid said in a video posted by the Chiefs.

Clark responded to the gesture on her Instagram Story with the message: “LETS GOOOOO ❤️❤️❤️❤️.”

The sneaker features a red-and-gold gradient upper, Clark’s “CC” logo , three metallic silver Swoosh designs, a gold No. 22 stitched into the laces and a matching gold outsole.

articles.title: Olivia Miles takes Caitlin Clark’s rookie record before Fever face their biggest test against Lynx
articles.standfirst: Indiana has an opportunity to demonstrate its playoff strength against the WNBA’s best team
articles.summary: Indiana has an opportunity to demonstrate its playoff strength against the WNBA’s best team
articles.body:
O livia Miles has taken one of Caitlin Clark’s most important WNBA records . The Minnesota Lynx guard surpassed the 769 points Clark scored during her historic 2024 rookie season, adding another chapter to the rapid rise of the league’s newest young star.

Miles broke the record Sunday while producing 21 points , six assists, three rebounds and two steals in Minnesota’s 101-89 victory over Connecticut . The performance took her season total to 790 points and helped the Lynx end a three-game losing streak.

Now Clark and the Indiana Fever face Miles’ Lynx in a game that could reveal how powerful they really are before the playoffs. Minnesota owns the WNBA’s best record at 32-10, while Indiana enters at 27-15 and remains trapped in a crowded battle for playoff positioning.

Caitlin Clark faces the WNBA’s strongest team without Olivia Miles

The highly anticipated individual matchup will not happen Tuesday night. Minnesota announced that Miles will miss the game with a left calf injury . The team has not revealed the severity of the problem or whether she could return when the Lynx and Fever meet again Thursday in Minneapolis.

Her absence does not make Minnesota an easy opponent. Napheesa Collier leads an experienced roster built to compete for a championship , and one victory in the final two games against Indiana would secure the No. 1 seed and home-court advantage throughout the playoffs.

Indiana needs a response after its painful 93-77 loss to Washington. Clark scored 25 points and recorded five assists, but she described the Fever’s defense as “pitiful.” Facing the league leader gives Indiana an immediate opportunity to show that the defeat was a warning rather than a sign of deeper problems.

Miles arrived in Minnesota as the No. 2 pick in the 2026 WNBA Draft after four seasons at Notre Dame and one at TCU. Her court vision, scoring ability and control of the offense quickly transformed her from a promising rookie into Minnesota’s leading scorer and one of the league’s most important young guards.

Taking Clark’s scoring record does not mean Miles has erased everything she accomplished. Clark still owns major rookie marks involving assists and three-point shooting , and she established her scoring total during a 40-game season, compared with the current 44-game schedule. But Miles has made one thing clear: Clark is no longer the only young guard capable of changing the WNBA’s record book.

articles.title: Caitlin Clark and Sophie Cunningham change the rules with their looks for the home finale
articles.standfirst: Indiana Fever says goodbye to Gainbridge Fieldhouse in the regular season.
articles.summary: Indiana Fever says goodbye to Gainbridge Fieldhouse in the regular season.
articles.body:
Gainbridge Fieldhouse is ready for a special night. Indiana Fever hosts Minnesota Lynx this Tuesday, September 22 , in its final regular-season game in front of its home crowd, just as the season begins to enter its most important stage.

Indiana enters the game with a 27-15 record , sitting fifth in the WNBA and already having secured a playoff spot. The team also boasts the league's highest scoring average, so the final game in Indianapolis comes with much more at stake than simply closing out the home schedule.

And while all of that is starting to take shape on the court, the players also made their mark before the game tipped off. Caitlin Clark and Sophie Cunningham arrived at the home finale in two looks that moved quite far away from their usual formulas .

Caitlin Clark traded jeans for a skirt

Clark often turns to jeans or pants for her arrivals, but this time she went with a completely different silhouette.

The player appeared in a black mini skirt, a gray sweater and black loafers . She also carried a black backpack and wore her prescription glasses, completing a simple outfit with a much more polished, preppy feel.

The change wasn't about wearing a lot of eye-catching pieces, but rather replacing an item that is usually part of her game-day looks with a skirt. That alone was enough to give her arrival a different feel .

Sophie Cunningham traded dresses for a more relaxed look

Sophie often leans toward dresses and more polished outfits, but this time she went with a much more relaxed formula.

The player arrived wearing what appear to be mini shorts, an oversized white sweatshirt , black open-toe heels and sunglasses. The combination mixed very casual pieces with a dressier touch in the shoes.

The sweatshirt also featured the phrase “kick rocks,” a detail that immediately stood out against the white fabric and gave the outfit its own edge.

But the change wasn't limited to their clothes. Both players arrive at this night after important seasons in Indiana, although in very different roles.

Clark has played 38 games, all as a starter, averaging 22.7 points, 8.4 assists, 3.9 rebounds, 1.0 steal and 0.5 blocks per game .

Cunningham, who returned to action after missing much of last season because of a knee injury, has contributed off the bench with 8.0 points, 2.3 rebounds, 1.2 assists and 0.6 steals per game .

Now, with the final home game about to begin and the playoffs getting closer, Caitlin Clark and Sophie Cunningham found two very different ways to arrive for a night that marks the end of one chapter and the beginning of another for Indiana Fever.

articles.title: Caitlin Clark reunites with Donna Kelce courtside and immediately embraces her as their Chiefs connection reaches Fever-Lynx game
articles.standfirst: The Indiana star immediately recognized “Mama Kelce” in the crowd and brought their friendship from the NFL’s biggest stage to the WNBA
articles.summary: The Indiana star immediately recognized “Mama Kelce” in the crowd and brought their friendship from the NFL’s biggest stage to the WNBA
articles.body:
C aitlin Clark did not need anyone to tell her that Donna Kelce was sitting courtside. As soon as the Indiana Fever star spotted the mother of Travis and Jason Kelce, she walked directly toward her and welcomed her with a warm embrace.

The moment felt less like a celebrity introduction and more like a reunion between two people who already shared a connection. Donna, affectionately known as “Mama Kelce,” smiled as Clark stopped beside her chair and took time to exchange a few words before returning to the court.

Their Chiefs connection reaches the WNBA

Donna attended the game between Indiana and the league-leading Minnesota Lynx. The Fever entered with a 27-15 record and needed a strong response in their fight for favorable playoff positioning, while Minnesota arrived at 32-10 with an opportunity to secure the No. 1 seed. Lynx rookie Olivia Miles missed the game with a left calf injury.

But Mama Kelce arrived wearing a Caitlin Clark shirt , ready to show her support and affection without hesitation. She knows exactly who she is rooting for.

Clark’s connection with the Kelce family grew from her lifelong support of the Kansas City Chiefs . Caitlin had previously watched Chiefs games from a VIP suite alongside Taylor Swift and members of the Kelce family, transforming her passion for the NFL into a genuine personal connection with some of the sport’s biggest names. Now, thanks to WNBA basketball, Donna Kelce is returning that support.

That connection became even more evident when Clark sent Chiefs head coach Andy Reid the first pair of her “Sea of Red” Nike Caitlin 1 shoes . Reid thanked her for the gesture with a heartwarming reaction in a video.

Caitlin Clark and the Indiana Fever are trying to enter the WNBA playoffs in the best possible position. At the same time, the Fever’s No. 22 is debuting her Nike signature shoes and generating priceless publicity by giving them to people she believes will genuinely treasure them, including Reid and her teammates. For now, Donna Kelce is fully supporting her from the front row.

articles.title: Cop pointed Taser directly at WNBA superstar Paige Bueckers during chaotic Arike Ogunbowale arrest
articles.standfirst: Newly released bodycam footage reveals the tense moments as police confronted Arike Ogunbowale, with Paige Bueckers caught in the middle of the chaotic arrest.
articles.summary: Newly released bodycam footage reveals the tense moments as police confronted Arike Ogunbowale, with Paige Bueckers caught in the middle of the chaotic arrest.
articles.body:
WNBA superstar Paige Bueckers experienced a moment of intense tension when a police officer aimed a Taser at her face during the chaotic arrest of her Dallas Wings teammate Arike Ogunbowale earlier this year, according to newly released bodycam footage obtained by the California Post .

The incident unfolded around 4:20 a.m. on March 5 outside the popular Miami nightclub E11EVEN . Bueckers, Ogunbowale , and several other WNBA players were inside celebrating Ogunbowale’s Unrivaled championship when the group was suddenly escorted toward the exit.

According to the police report, after an altercation inside the club, Ogunbowale and her companions were being led out a back exit when she allegedly punched a security guard in the face with a closed fist. Once the alleged victim identified her as the aggressor, an officer attempted to detain her as she left the venue.

articles.title: Caitlin Clark faces Bri January’s aggressive gesture as fans try to decode what she yelled
articles.standfirst: The tense courtside exchange overshadowed part of Clark’s dominant performance against the Minnesota Lynx
articles.summary: The tense courtside exchange overshadowed part of Clark’s dominant performance against the Minnesota Lynx
articles.body:
Caitlin Clark was in the middle of another impressive performance when an uncomfortable exchange with Indiana Fever assistant coach Bri January suddenly drew attention. January approached Clark during a break in the action, gestured forcefully and appeared to yell something directly at the star guard.

Clark listened briefly before responding and walking away. The audio does not clearly reveal what January said, but some fans attempting to read her lips became convinced that her first words were: “Stay away from me.” That interpretation remains speculation and has not been confirmed by January, Clark or the Fever.

Fans question Bri January’s message to Caitlin Clark

The intensity of January’s gesture made the moment difficult to ignore. Social media users questioned why the assistant coach appeared so angry with Clark, particularly while the Fever guard was producing a strong all-around performance against the team with the WNBA’s best record.

Clark eventually finished with 27 points , nine assists and seven rebounds, coming close to another triple-double. Indiana defeated Minnesota 96-77 to improve to 28-15 and keep alive its hopes of securing home-court advantage in the playoffs.

January is not an unknown member of Indiana’s staff. The former Fever guard helped the franchise win the 2012 WNBA championship and now works as one of Stephanie White’s assistant coaches. She has previously been seen having intense conversations with Clark, including another timeout exchange that generated criticism from fans.

Strong communication between a coach and a superstar is normal during an important game, but the body language made this interaction appear more personal to viewers . Until either woman explains what was said, the supposed “stay away from me” message remains unverified even as the mysterious moment continues to generate questions.

articles.title: “I need help paying the bills”: Inside the chaotic, multimillion-dollar divorce that is casting a shadow over Brittney Griner's season
articles.standfirst: Griner and the Connecticut Sun have just 10 wins through 43 WNBA games.
articles.summary: Griner and the Connecticut Sun have just 10 wins through 43 WNBA games.
articles.body:
Brittney Griner ’s divorce is adding another layer of uncertainty to a difficult WNBA season, with her estranged wife asking the court to consider the stark gap between their incomes when deciding support. The Connecticut Sun star filed for divorce in Fulton County, Georgia , after eight years of marriage, while Cherelle Griner has asked the court for financial support and joint legal custody of their two-year-old son.

Cherelle says the marriage ended on July 24 and describes it as “irretrievably broken with no hope for reconciliation,” whilst she also notes that Brittney earns substantially more than she does. In court documents, she says there is a “substantial disparity” in their income and that she is “unable to meet her reasonable financial needs on a monthly basis without continued support.” Brittney is playing for the Sun on a reported one-year contract worth more than $1 million, placing her earnings at the center of the request as the divorce case moves forward. Cherelle , who is an attorney, also wants joint legal custody of Bash , with the court determining physical custody and parenting time according to the child’s best interests.

Sun slump to latest defeat as dismal WNBA season continues

The developments come at a bad time for Brittney as her first season with Connecticut has also been a difficult one, with the Sun sitting at 10-33 after Tuesday’s loss to the Washington Mystics . Shakira Austin scored 25 points and grabbed 13 rebounds as the Mystics defeated Connecticut 79-69 on September 22 . Diamond Miller led Connecticut with 19 points, whilst Leila Lacan and Raegan Beers each scored 11. Washington used a 15-4 run to build a double-digit lead late in the third quarter. The result left Connecticut with 10 wins and 33 losses, while Washington improved to 27-16 and secured a franchise-record 27th victory. Neither team’s immediate fortunes erase the off-court drama. The Sun will now host the Toronto Tempo on September 24 in the regular-season finale for both teams, with neither side qualifying for the postseason as Connecticut prepare to relocate to Texas to become the Houston Comets . The team had reached the WNBA Semifinals in 2024, but this season has taken a very different path as they prepare to close the campaign with a second successive losing record. The team finished 11-33 in 2025 and will finish at best 11-33 in 2026. For Griner , the divorce proceedings now add a separate legal and financial issue to an already challenging season.

articles.title: WNBA Playoffs 2026: Start day, key dates, format, and current playoff picture
articles.standfirst: The Lynx have locked up No. 1, with seven other teams set to battle for the 2026 title
articles.summary: The Lynx have locked up No. 1, with seven other teams set to battle for the 2026 title
articles.body:
The 2026 WNBA playoffs are almost here, with the regular season entering its final days and the eight-team postseason field already determined.

The Minnesota Lynx have secured the No. 1 seed, making them the first team to officially lock in a playoff position. It’s the second consecutive postseason in which Minnesota has finished atop the league, as Olivia Miles, Napheesa Collier and the rest of the Lynx look to bring another championship to Minnesota.

The Lynx will be joined in the postseason by the Golden State Valkyries, Las Vegas Aces, Atlanta Dream, Indiana Fever, Washington Mystics, Dallas Wings and New York Liberty. While all eight teams have qualified, their final positions in the standings haven’t been completely settled entering Sept. 23.

The Valkyries and defending champion Aces are competing for the No. 2 and No. 3 seeds, while the Dream and Fever remain in contention for fourth. The middle of the bracket could also change, with the Fever, Mystics, Wings and Liberty all involved in a battle for their eventual postseason positions.

The regular season is scheduled to conclude on Sept. 24, meaning the final bracket will be determined just days before the playoffs begin. That leaves very little time for teams to prepare for their opening series.

How the 2026 WNBA playoff format works

The 2026 postseason begins Sunday, Sept. 27, with first-round action starting at 2 p.m. ET. Unlike some other major sports leagues, the WNBA doesn’t divide its playoff field by conference. Instead, the eight teams with the best regular-season records qualify and are seeded from No. 1 through No. 8.

The opening round features four best-of-three series: No. 1 plays No. 8, No. 2 faces No. 7, No. 3 meets No. 6 and No. 4 takes on No. 5. The higher seed has home-court advantage in Game 1 and, if necessary, Game 3, while the lower seed hosts Game 2.

The bracket also remains fixed throughout the postseason. Teams won’t be reseeded after the opening round, which means the path to the Finals will be determined by the original bracket.

After the first round, the semifinals switch to a best-of-five format. Those series use a 2-2-1 setup, with the higher seed hosting Games 1 and 2 and a potential Game 5.

The WNBA Finals are then played as a best-of-seven series. The higher seed hosts Games 1 and 2, as well as Games 5 and 7 if either is necessary.

The first-round series are scheduled to begin Sept. 27, with Game 2s following on Sept. 29 and 30. If deciding games are needed, Game 3s are scheduled for Oct. 1 and 2. The semifinals are set to begin Oct. 4, while the Finals are scheduled to tip off Oct. 17.

Minnesota is the only team with a confirmed seed at this time. The remaining positions will be settled during the final regular-season games, setting the stage for a postseason featuring eight teams chasing the 2026 WNBA championship.

articles.summary: A top-seeded Atlanta Dream visits the battle-tested New York Liberty
articles.body:
The 2026 WNBA Playoffs are a couple days away but at the Barclays Center, two E astern Conference heavyweights collide with the season's calculus turned upside down.

The New York Liberty host the Atlanta Dream on Wednesday night for a star-studded game before the last rounds of the 2026 season

What time is the Atlanta vs New York game and how to watch it live?

The Atlanta and New York teams are playing this wednesday, September 23, with tip-off scheduled for 8:00 p.m. ET (7:00 p.m. Central Time and 5:00 p.m. Pacific Time). As for the game’s live broadcast, you’ll be able to watch it on TV through NBCSN and on Peacock in streaming.

Atlanta Dream and New York Liberty: Two Roads to the Same Stage

Atlanta arrives as the Eastern Conference's top seed , closing the regular season with a 28–14 record and a plus-273 point differential — the best mark in the conference. New York finished third in the East at 26–16 (plus-168), a step behind but riding a resurgence that saw them look every bit like the deep, versatile roster that has come to define the franchise.

The Dream capped their season with a pair of blowouts, thrashing the Connecticut Sun 103–59 on September 17 and burying the Chicago Sky 106–81 on September 19. The Liberty answered emphatically, downing the Minnesota Lynx 93–81 on the road and then demolishing the Toronto Tempo 106–69 on September 20. This is a first-round series between two clubs peaking at exactly the right moment.

Deep dive in the Atlanta Dream vs New York Liberty game of the regular season: Firepower vs Star Power

The most telling numbers come straight from each team's regular-season finale. In New York's 106–69 rout of Toronto, the Liberty carved up the defense with 29 assists on 39 made field goals, shooting a searing 56% from the floor and 43% from three (16-of-37).

They controlled the glass 36–26 and blocked seven shots. It was a clinic in ball movement — the kind of collective offense that makes the Liberty so difficult to game-plan against over a series.

Atlanta's finale was every bit as emphatic. In the 106–81 win over Chicago, the Dream shot 52% from the field, drained 13 threes at a 50% clip (13-of-26), and dominated possession, leading for nearly 27 of the 40 minutes and building a 27-point cushion.

Thirteen steals underscored the disruptive, high-energy defense that carried Atlanta to the top seed.

The strategic subplot is clear: New York's balanced, pass-heavy attack against Atlanta's blend of perimeter shooting and defensive pressure. Whichever team dictates tempo — and controls the turnover battle — will hold the edge.

The Liberty are built around a formidable core. Guard Sabrina Ionescu orchestrates the offense, while two-time champion forward Breanna Stewart anchors both ends. Add forward Satou Sabally, German international Leonie Fiebich, and center Jonquel Jones in the frontcourt, and New York can attack from every position on the floor. French guard Marine Johannes offers scoring punch off the bench.

Atlanta counters with a dynamic backcourt led by Allisha Gray and Rhyne Howard , the twin engines of the Dream's perimeter game. Up front, Angel Reese brings relentless rebounding and interior energy, with veteran center Brionna Jones and the experienced DeWanna Bonner rounding out a rotation that mixes youth and playoff-tested savvy. Guard Jordin Canada adds pace and defensive bite in the halfcourt.

What is the prediction for the Atlanta Dream vs New York Liberty game?

This has the makings of a genuine coin-flip, with two teams entering on emphatic winning notes. Atlanta's top seed and superior point differential give them a slight edge on paper, but New York's home floor and proven ability to topple the league's best complicate the picture. Expect a high-scoring, physical contest decided in the final minutes. The pick: New York Liberty to take the win at the Barclays Center, with Atlanta's depth ensuring a long fight.

articles.summary: The Indiana Fever teammates are very close and that could continue off the WNBA court.
articles.body:
It hasn't quite been the stellar season some were expecting for the Indiana Fever , but they've been extremely competitive in a tough Top 8. Currently sitting in fifth place with a 28-15 record , they aren't that far off the top team in the WNBA , the Minnesota Lynx at 32-11 .

As expected, the team has been paced by their Big 3 of Caitlin Clark , Kelsey Mitchell , and Aliyah Boston . Those three have been supported by a strong cast of role players, the most notorious of which are Sophie Cunningham and Lexie Hull . While Monique Billings and Makayla Timpson have been key as well, the other two have a strong friendship with Clark that has spanned a couple of years now.

Cunningham, of course, has made headlines off the court with her gameday looks as well as her podcast - which has led to some unwanted negativity. Hull is a bit less out there publicly and more focused on basketball , more akin to Clark. But even Hull recently admitted that she's considered dabbling in the podcast space - just not with Clark.

Lexie Hull reveals she discussed a potential show with Sophie Cunningham

Instead, Hull seems to prefer a potential collaboration with Cunningham . While speaking to Athlon Sports , Hull mentioned that she's discussed the possibility with Cunningham, and it might happen in the future.

It’s funny, Sophie and I joked about doing something together, which would have been fun. But yeah, it’s just fun to watch her do that... Yeah, I think it’s a fun thing to do. But right now, I just don’t have the time. I enjoy being a guest on others’ [podcasts], though. It’s fun to get to go and have interesting conversations and fun conversations. And for now, I’ll stay as a guest, but maybe down the line. We’ll see.

It wouldn't surprise anyone to see Cunningham and Hull launch a joint show at some point. Clark would likely be one of their first guests; if she's even up for it.
